date_note: Date of the digi.no article; the page gives no earlier day for the data listing. FLC registered the intrusion late on 11 October, per the article.
title: Barracuda group claims theft of Femern link contractor FLC data, offers it for sale
summary: A hacker group called Barracuda has put 2.44 terabytes of data about the Femern project and the contractor FLC up for sale for 500.000 dollars, digi.no reports. Barracuda told Ingeniøren it is behind the attack. FLC registered the intrusion late on 11 October, then shut its internet connection and asked all staff to turn off their computers.
plain: A hacker group says it stole data from the company building the Femern link and wants to sell it. The company says it detected a break-in on 11 October.
exec: A major infrastructure contractor reports an intrusion and a group claims to be selling its data, which is a supplier-exposure risk.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Only the start of the article could be read, and no advice from FLC was seen.

evidence.quote: En hackergruppe kalt Barracuda har lagt ut 2,44 terabytes data om Femern-projektet og entreprenøren FLC til salgs for 500.000 dollar.

validation.note: Single publisher (digi.no, byline Ingeniøren). The page is paywalled and only the opening paragraphs were read; the sale listing and the group's authorship are Barracuda's own claim. FLC's own statement was not read.
